docs.title: 1. Continue config.json (VS Code)
docs.text: Location - macOS/Linux: ~/.continue/config.json - Windows: %APPDATA%\Continue\config.json

docs.title: Full Example with Multiple Models & Django System Prompt
docs.text:
{
  "models": [
    {
      "title": "Gemma 3 4B (Chat – Main)",
      "provider": "ollama",
      "model": "gemma3:4b",
      "apiBase": "http://localhost:11434",
      "systemMessage": "You are a senior Django expert. Follow Django best practices, use the ORM correctly, and never suggest raw SQL unless explicitly asked. Keep responses concise and include code examples when relevant.",
      "options": {
        "num_ctx": 4096,
        "temperature": 0.7
      }
    },
    {
      "title": "Qwen3 4B (Fallback – Faster)",
      "provider": "ollama",
      "model": "qwen3:4b",
      "apiBase": "http://localhost:11434",
      "options": {
        "num_ctx": 2048,
        "temperature": 0.5
      }
    }
  ],
  "tabAutocompleteModel": {
    "title": "Llama 3.2 1B (Fast Autocomplete)",
    "provider": "ollama",
    "model": "llama3.2:1b",
    "apiBase": "http://localhost:11434"
  },
  "embeddingsProvider": {
    "provider": "ollama",
    "model": "nomic-embed-text",
    "apiBase": "http://localhost:11434"
  },
  "contextProviders": [
    {
      "name": "codebase",
      "params": {}
    },
    {
      "name": "folder",
      "params": {
        "path": "docs"
      }
    }
  ],
  "allowAnonymousTelemetry": false
}

docs.title: Explanation of Fields
docs.text: Field Description models Array of chat models you can select from the Continue sidebar. title Display name in VS Code. provider Always "ollama" for local models. model Exact name you used in ollama pull. apiBase Ollama’s default endpoint. systemMessage Prepended instructions for the assistant (great for Django‑specific behaviour). options Model‑specific parameters: num_ctx (context window size in tokens), temperature (randomness). tabAutocompleteModel Separate model for inline code completion – use a tiny 1B model for speed. embeddingsProvider Required for @codebase context. Use nomic-embed-text (pull it: ollama pull nomic-embed-text). contextProviders Enable @codebase (whole project) and @folder docs (documentation folder). allowAnonymousTelemetry Set to false for complete privacy.

docs.title: Performance Tuning for 8GB RAM
docs.text:
• Reduce context window for the chat model: "num_ctx": 2048 (or even 1024).
  • Use a 1B autocomplete model as shown above.
  • Close other heavy applications (browser tabs, Docker, Slack).

docs.title: 2. AI Customizer ai/config.json
docs.text: Generated automatically on first run of ai_customizer.py. Edit to change behaviour.

docs.title: Field Reference
docs.text:
Field Description Default model Ollama model name to use for all tasks. gemma3:4b temperature Sampling temperature (0 = deterministic, 1 = creative). 0.7 num_ctx Context window size in tokens (higher = more memory). 4096 system_prompt Base instructions for the assistant (prepended to every prompt). "You are a senior Django developer..." priority_patterns Glob patterns for --priority file search. Order = priority. ["*.py", "*/models.py", ...] exclude_patterns Glob patterns to ignore when searching files. ["*/migrations/*", "*/__pycache__/*", ...]

After editing, restart ai_customizer.py for changes to take effect.

docs.title: 3. Environment Variables (Ollama)
docs.text:
Set these before starting Ollama to tweak its behaviour globally.

Variable Purpose Example OLLAMA_HOST Change bind address (default 127.0.0.1:11434). export OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 OLLAMA_ORIGINS Allow web origins (for local web apps). export OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*" OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE How long to keep models loaded after last use (default 5m). Set to -1 to stay loaded forever. export OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=10m OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL Number of parallel requests (default 1). export OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2

docs.title: How to Use Environment Variables
docs.text:
Start Ollama with variables set:

export OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=10m
ollama serve

Or, if running as a systemd service, edit the service file:

sudo systemctl edit ollama

Add:

[Service]
Environment="OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=10m"
Environment="OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2"

Then restart: sudo systemctl restart ollama.

docs.title: 4. Project Environment (.env) for Makefile & Task Runner
docs.text:
Your project root should contain a .env file (see example below). This file is used by the Makefile and the task runner to locate directories and set defaults.

# .env – AI Assistant environment
OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434
OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=5m
DEFAULT_MODEL=gemma3:4b
FAST_MODEL=llama3.2:1b

PROJECT_ROOT=$(pwd)
AI_DIR=ai
DOCS_AI_DIR=docs/ai
TASKS_DIR=$(DOCS_AI_DIR)/tasks
CHANGELOG_DIR=$(AI_DIR)/changelogs

WEBSITES=ctc-research lms-demo vresume
PRIORITY_PATTERNS=*.py */models.py */views.py */serializers.py
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=*/migrations/* */__pycache__/* .git/* $(AI_DIR)/* $(DOCS_AI_DIR)/*/reports/*

Note: Do not commit secrets (like API keys) to this file if you use version control.

docs.title: 5. Task Prompts
docs.text:
Task prompt files are markdown documents (.md) placed in docs/ai/tasks/. Each file contains a system‑like instruction that the AI follows when you run make task-run NAME=<task>. The first line of the file becomes a short description in make task-list.

  • analyze_project.md – full project analysis with N+1 and duplication detection
  • comprehensive_analysis.md – phased analysis with package check and report generation
  • fix_n_plus_one.md, remove_duplications.md, refactor_context.md – follow‑up fixes
  • uniform_docs.md – standardise all markdown files
  • merge_styles.md, replace_pattern.md, refactor_design_pattern.md – code transformations

Create your own by copying an existing task file and modifying the instructions.

docs.title: 6. Quick Setup Summary
docs.text:
1. Install Ollama and pull models: 

    ollama pull gemma3:4b
ollama pull llama3.2:1b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

  2. Configure Continue – replace ~/.continue/config.json with the full example above.

  3. Restart VS Code.

  4. Copy the .env example into your project root and adjust paths.

  5. Run ai_customizer.py once to generate ai/config.json, then edit it to your liking.

  6. (Optional) Set environment variables for persistent model loading.

All done – you now have a production‑ready, fully private AI assistant for Django.

docs.title: AI Customizer Script
docs.text:
The ai_customizer.py script gives you full control over your local AI assistant from the terminal. It allows:

  • Priority‑based file search (@search keyword)
  • Inject documentation as context (@docs)
  • Log every conversation and task as snake_case markdown changelogs
  • Custom model parameters (temperature, context size, system prompt)

docs.title: 1. Save the Script
docs.text: Create a file named ai_customizer.py in your project root with the content below (copy the full script from the end of this document).

docs.title: 2. Make it Executable (macOS/Linux)
docs.text: chmod +x ai_customizer.py

docs.title: 3. Run Interactive Chat
docs.text: ./ai_customizer.py

docs.title: Commands inside the chat
docs.text: Command Action @docs Loads your entire docs/ folder as context for the next question. @search keyword Finds files containing keyword, lets you select one, and loads its content into context. save Saves the current conversation to ai/changelogs/chat_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_slug.md. exit Quits.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
You: @docs What are Django signal best practices?
AI: (answers using your documentation)

You: @search get_absolute_url
🔍 Found 2 files...
Enter number: 1
Loaded blog/models.py into context.

You: Explain the get_absolute_url method.
AI: (explains your actual code)

You: save
Conversation saved to ai/changelogs/chat_20260613_152030_get_absolute_url.md

docs.title: 4. Single Task Mode
docs.text:
./scripts/ai_customizer.py --task "write a Django model for a shopping cart" --priority --with-docs
  • --priority – interactively select files based on priority patterns.
  • --with-docs – include documentation as context.

The response is printed and also saved to ai/changelogs/task_...md.

Now you have a powerful terminal‑based AI assistant that respects your project structure and logs everything.

docs.title: Latest AI, MCP, and package feature inventory
docs.text: This is the compact attachment for repository-aware AI agents. Keep it aligned with core/libs/ceptor-ai/src/ceptor_ai/mcp_server.py, applications/kilo/config.json, and docs/ai/mcp_reference.md.

docs.title: Current MCP endpoints
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Mutation risk /health Readiness check for local clients Read-only /info ceptor-ai package metadata Read-only /features Feature inventory and canonical paths Read-only /file-structure Package, docs, and Kilo path map Read-only /auth/features Detect optional auth integrations Read-only; no secrets /django-fusion/info Optional package metadata Read-only /django-fusion/components Component registry summary Read-only /django-fusion/viewsets Viewset availability Read-only /websites/endpoints Configured site endpoint map Read-only /ssl/status Certificate presence and expiry summary Read-only; no private keys /proxy/status Proxy configuration presence Read-only

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
# Run from the repository root.
uv pip install -e core/libs/ceptor-ai/
uv pip install -e 'core/libs/ceptor-ai/[mcp]'
PYTHONPATH=core/libs/ceptor-ai/src \
  uvicorn ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8002

Kilo uses the same app and environment in applications/kilo/config.json. Keep the server bound to loopback for local development. A shared deployment requires authentication, an explicit owner, and documented network controls.

docs.title: Agent operating contract
docs.text:
Before using MCP, an agent should:

  1. Read root and nested AGENTS.md instructions.
  2. Call /health, then /features and /file-structure.
  3. Use canonical paths returned by the server instead of guessed legacy paths.
  4. Ask for approval before editing files or changing MCP configuration.
  5. Never send API keys, cookies, private keys, or full environment files to MCP.
  6. Treat all current endpoints as metadata-only; do not infer write capability.

Suggested setup prompt:

Set up the local Structa Cloud ceptor-ai MCP server. Read the root AGENTS.md, the applicable library instructions, docs/ai/mcp_reference.md, and this feature inventory. Install the editable package with the mcp extra; start ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app on 127.0.0.1:8002 with PYTHONPATH=core/libs/ceptor-ai/src; verify /health, /features, and /file-structure; then report results. Do not expose the port, reveal secrets, mutate files, or add Django/Wagtail imports to ceptor_ai.

docs.title: Canonical attachment set
docs.text:
docs/ai/
├── README.md
├── START_HERE.md
├── latest_features.md
├── mcp_reference.md
├── customizer.md
├── setup.md
└── tasks/

applications/kilo/
├── config.json
├── kilo.jsonc
├── commands/ceptor-ai.md
└── skills/

core/libs/ceptor-ai/
├── AGENTS.md
├── PROMPTS.md
├── QUICKSTART.md
├── README.md
└── src/ceptor_ai/
    ├── cli.py
    └── mcp_server.py

core/libs/django-fusion/
├── AGENTS.md
├── PROMPTS.md
├── README.md
└── docs/

docs.title: Maintenance checklist
docs.text:
• Update MCP_FEATURES and this file together when the public endpoint inventory changes.
  • Update the setup prompt and Kilo command when the launch command, port, or environment changes.
  • Keep ceptor_ai importable without Django settings; optional integrations must remain behind find_spec/import_module.
  • Run cd core/libs/ceptor-ai && uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_metadata.py after MCP metadata changes.

docs.title: MCP reference and setup prompt
docs.text: This page is the source of truth for the local Model Context Protocol (MCP) workflow used by Structa Cloud AI tools. The current server is a small HTTP metadata app owned by ceptor-ai; it is intended for local, trusted clients and must not be exposed publicly without authentication and network controls.

docs.title: Canonical server
docs.text:
• Application: ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app
  • Source: core/libs/ceptor-ai/src/ceptor_ai/mcp_server.py
  • Optional dependency: fastapi and uvicorn from the mcp extra
  • Bind address: 127.0.0.1 (local-only by default)
  • Port: 8002
  • Kilo entry: applications/kilo/config.json

Install and start it from the repository root:

uv pip install -e core/libs/ceptor-ai/
uv pip install -e 'core/libs/ceptor-ai/[mcp]'
PYTHONPATH=core/libs/ceptor-ai/src \
  uvicorn ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8002

The same setup as a copy/paste prompt for an AI assistant:

Configure the local Structa Cloud ceptor-ai MCP server. First read AGENTS.md, docs/ai/START_HERE.md, docs/ai/latest_features.md, and core/libs/ceptor-ai/AGENTS.md. From the repository root, install the editable package and its mcp extra. Launch ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app with PYTHONPATH=core/libs/ceptor-ai/src, bound to 127.0.0.1:8002. Verify /health, /info, /features, and /file-structure with curl. Do not bind to 0.0.0.0, expose the port through a proxy, send secrets in prompts, or add Django/Wagtail imports to the standalone ceptor_ai MCP module. Report the exact command, endpoint results, and any missing optional packages before editing configuration.

docs.title: Kilo configuration
docs.text:
applications/kilo/config.json contains the HTTP MCP entry used by Kilo:

{
  "ceptor-ai": {
    "command": "uvicorn",
    "args": [
      "ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app",
      "--host", "127.0.0.1",
      "--port", "8002"
    ],
    "env": {
      "PYTHONPATH": "core/libs/ceptor-ai/src"
    }
  }
}

Run a smoke test before opening Kilo:

curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8002/health
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8002/info
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8002/features
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8002/file-structure

docs.title: Endpoint contract
docs.text: Endpoint Use Safe behavior GET /health Readiness check Does not require Django settings. GET /info Package/import metadata Mirrors the CLI metadata function. GET /features Current MCP feature inventory Use to discover capabilities before a task. GET /file-structure Canonical package/docs/Kilo paths Prefer these paths over guessed paths. GET /auth/features Optional auth package detection Reports availability, not credentials. GET /django-fusion/info Optional library metadata May return unavailable when the package is absent. GET /django-fusion/components Component registry summary Read-only introspection. GET /django-fusion/viewsets Viewset availability Read-only introspection. GET /websites/endpoints Site host/port map Configuration metadata only. GET /ssl/status Certificate presence/expiry summary Never returns private keys. GET /proxy/status Proxy configuration presence Does not mutate proxy files.

docs.title: Safety and maintenance rules
docs.text:
1. Keep the server importable without Django settings. Optional integrations must use importlib.util.find_spec and importlib.import_module.
  2. Treat every endpoint as read-only metadata. Do not add file writes, shell execution, database mutations, or secret/config values to responses.
  3. Update MCP_FEATURES, this page, and docs/ai/latest_features.md together whenever an endpoint or public capability changes.
  4. Keep paths rooted at the current monorepo layout: core/libs/, applications/kilo/, and docs/ai/.
  5. Run core/libs/ceptor-ai metadata tests after changes.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• ModuleNotFoundError: ceptor_ai: run from the repository root and set PYTHONPATH=core/libs/ceptor-ai/src, or install the editable package.
  • Error loading ASGI app: install the MCP extra and confirm the target is ceptor_ai.mcp_server:app, not the old .kilo or mcp_server:app path.
  • Connection refused: start uvicorn first and confirm port 8002 is free.
  • Optional package unavailable: this is expected for integrations that are not installed; /health, /info, /features, and /file-structure should still work.
  • Kilo sees stale data: restart the local MCP process and re-run /features.

docs.title: Interactive Tasks with Prompt Files
docs.text:
You can feed a custom prompt file (e.g., project_analysis_prompt.txt) to your local Ollama model and then have an interactive conversation where the AI follows that prompt as a persistent instruction. This is useful for:

  • Project analysis (e.g., checking alignment with Ollama best practices)
  • Code review with specific guidelines
  • Generating documentation from a template
  • Role‑playing a specific expert (Django security, Docker optimisation, etc.)

docs.title: Method 1: Using ai_customizer.py (Recommended)
docs.text: Your ai_customizer.py script supports a persistent system_prompt defined in ai/config.json. To load a prompt file:

docs.title: Step‑by‑step
docs.text:
1. Place your prompt file somewhere in your project, e.g.: 

    docs/ai/prompts/project_analysis_prompt.txt

  2. Edit ai/config.json in your project root and set the system_prompt field to the full content of the prompt file.

You can do this manually (copy‑paste) or use a small script:

#!/bin/bash
# set-prompt.sh
PROMPT=$(cat docs/ai/prompts/project_analysis_prompt.txt)
jq --arg sp "$PROMPT" '.system_prompt = $sp' ai/config.json > ai/config.tmp && mv ai/config.tmp ai/config.json
  1. Run interactive chat: 
    ./ai_customizer.py

Now every question you ask will be answered according to the loaded prompt.

  1. To switch between different prompts, keep multiple prompt files and re‑run the script before starting ai_customizer.py.

docs.title: Example: Analysing a Project
docs.text:
Assume you have a prompt file project_analysis_prompt.txt that instructs the AI to act as an expert in Ollama best practices. After setting it as the system_prompt, you can:

You: Here is my project tree:
.
├── docker-compose.yml
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
└── myapp/
    ├── models.py
    └── views.py

What improvements would you suggest based on Ollama's documentation?

The AI will respond with a structured report as defined in your prompt.

docs.title: Method 2: Using Continue’s systemMessage (VS Code)
docs.text: If you prefer to work inside VS Code’s Continue chat, you can add the prompt as a systemMessage in your ~/.continue/config.json.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Read your prompt file and escape it for JSON (or copy‑paste directly).

  2. Add a new model entry:

{
  "models": [
    {
      "title": "Project Analyzer (Gemma)",
      "provider": "ollama",
      "model": "gemma3:4b",
      "apiBase": "http://localhost:11434",
      "systemMessage": "You are an expert AI assistant... (paste the full prompt here)"
    }
  ],
  "tabAutocompleteModel": { ... }
}
  1. Restart VS Code, open Continue, select “Project Analyzer” from the model dropdown, and start chatting. The AI will follow the prompt for the whole conversation.

💡 This method keeps your global ai/config.json unchanged – useful if you also use ai_customizer.py for other tasks.

docs.title: Method 3: Direct ollama run with Pre‑loaded Prompt (One‑off)
docs.text: For a quick, non‑persistent session, you can pipe the prompt file into ollama run and then continue interactively.

docs.title: Example (Linux/macOS)
docs.text:
# Start with the prompt as the first message
cat project_analysis_prompt.txt | ollama run gemma3:4b --interactive

The --interactive flag keeps the session open so you can ask follow‑up questions. However, the prompt will not be re‑sent automatically; you may need to repeat it or rely on the model’s memory (limited by context window).

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep prompts concise but specific – 500–2000 words is ideal.
  • Store prompts in docs/ai/prompts/ for version control.
  • Use the ai/config.json method for daily work – it’s the most reliable.
  • Combine with @docs and @search in ai_customizer.py to provide real project files as context.

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text:
• Configuration Reference – for editing ai/config.json and Continue settings.
  • AI Customizer Script – full reference for the interactive CLI.
  • Troubleshooting – if the model doesn’t behave as expected.

Now you can turn any task prompt into a persistent, interactive AI assistant – completely local and private.

docs.text: Complete reference for all AI tasks available via make task-run NAME=<task> and the ai_customizer.py CLI.

docs.title: Task File Format
docs.text:
Each task is a .md file in docs/ai/tasks/. The first line is the short description shown in make task-list.

Analyze all Django views for N+1 query patterns.

## Instructions

1. Search all `views.py` files in the monorepo
2. For each QuerySet call, check if related objects are accessed in a loop
3. Flag any `for obj in queryset: obj.related.all()` patterns
4. Output: file path, line number, suggested fix

| File | Line | Pattern | Fix |

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution Ollama not found Ensure Ollama is running. On Windows, check system tray. On Ubuntu: sudo systemctl status ollama. Continue cannot connect curl http://localhost:11434 – if fails, restart Ollama. Also check firewall. Slow autocomplete Use a 1B model for autocomplete (llama3.2:1b). Reduce context window to 2048. VS Code freezes / memory error Reduce num_ctx to 1024. Close other applications. Restart VS Code. Model responses are garbled Remove and re‑pull: ollama rm gemma3:4b ; ollama pull gemma3:4b Django server slows down Stop the model when not in use (quit Ollama). Restart when needed. ai_customizer.py says “ollama: command not found” Ollama must be in PATH. On macOS/Linux, restart terminal. On Windows, add C:\Program Files\Ollama to PATH. @docs loads nothing Ensure you have a docs/ folder with .md files. The script looks for docs/ relative to current working directory.

docs.title: Windows Specific
docs.text:
• Use PowerShell instead of CMD.
  • If curl is missing, test Ollama by opening http://localhost:11434 in a browser.
  • To run Python scripts: python ai_customizer.py (if .py not associated).

docs.title: Ubuntu Specific
docs.text:
• Add your user to the ollama group: sudo usermod -aG ollama $USER then log out/in.
  • Restart service: sudo systemctl restart ollama

docs.title: Task: Deep Project Analysis with Duplication & N+1 Detection
docs.text:
You are an expert Django architect. Analyse the project and produce a structured report with:

  1. Context mapping – use‑case variables, shared contexts, duplications.
  2. Duplications – exact duplicates in Python, templates, JS.
  3. N+1 query problems – missing select_related/prefetch_related.
  4. Category‑wise changes – separate for assets/js, templates, python with priority (High/Medium/Low).
  5. TODO comments – one per issue, with file, line, description, fix, priority.
  6. Recommended tasks – suggest fix_n_plus_one, remove_duplications, refactor_context.
  7. Bot section – alternative perspective.

docs.title: Report format (strict)
docs.text: ```markdown

docs.title: Python
docs.text: • file:line – duplicate code. TODO: extract to shared function.

docs.title: 3. N+1 Query Problems
docs.text: • view_name – line X. TODO: add select_related('field').

docs.title: 🔴 High
docs.text: • Python: ...

docs.title: TODO (High): fix N+1 in product_list – add select_related('category')
6. Recommended Tasks
docs.text:
• fix_n_plus_one
  • remove_duplications
  • refactor_context

docs.title: 7. Bot Opinion
docs.text: ... After the report, ask: "Which priority would you like to act on first? (1=High, 2=Medium, 3=Low)" and suggest the corresponding task.

docs.title: Task: Comprehensive Django Analysis with Phased Actions
docs.text: You are an expert Django architect and automation engineer. Perform a phased analysis of the project, following the steps below. At the end, output a report saved to ai/reports/comprehensive_analysis_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.md and within the same file list the recommended phases for action.

docs.title: Phase 0: Environment & Package Check
docs.text:
• Determine the project root directory.
  • List installed packages from requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / Pipfile.
  • Identify missing common packages: django-extensions, django-debug-toolbar, pytest-django, celery, django-rest-framework (if used).
  • If a package is missing but would help with the tasks below, note it in the report with a suggested install command.

docs.title: Phase 1: File & Structure Mapping
docs.text:
• Scan the project root and all subdirectories.
  • Identify all Django apps (directories containing models.py, views.py, urls.py).
  • Map file types:
  • *.py – Django logic
  • *.html – templates
  • *.js – frontend (in assets/js/ or static/)
  • *.css / *.scss
  • Note any unusual or misplaced files.

docs.title: Phase 2: Code Quality & Pattern Analysis
docs.text:
• Detect design patterns used (MVC, Repository, Factory, etc.).
  • Locate code duplications (same function/class across multiple files).
  • Find N+1 query candidates (loops with ORM access without select_related).
  • Identify missing type hints, docstrings, and overly complex functions.

docs.title: Phase 3: Django‑Specific Issue Detection
docs.text:
• Check settings.py for:
  • DEBUG = True in production‑like environment
  • SECRET_KEY hardcoded
  • ALLOWED_HOSTS misconfiguration
  • Missing STATIC_ROOT, MEDIA_ROOT
  • Check urls.py for missing app_name or improper include.
  • Scan for raw SQL usage (raw(), execute()).
  • Find views without login required where needed.

docs.title: Phase 4: Generate Report (Markdown)
docs.text:
Save a markdown report in ai/reports/comprehensive_analysis_<timestamp>.md with the following sections:

```markdown

docs.title: Phase 0: Packages & Environment
docs.text:
• Installed packages (list)
  • Missing suggested packages (with install commands)

docs.title: Phase 1: Structure
docs.text:
• Root directory tree (abbreviated)
  • Apps discovered

docs.title: Phase 2: Code Quality
docs.text:
• Duplications (list with file:line)
  • N+1 candidates
  • Missing type hints / docstrings

docs.title: Phase 3: Django Issues
docs.text:
• Settings problems
  • Raw SQL usage
  • Auth/security issues

docs.title: Phase 4: Recommended Phases (Actions)
docs.text:
Each action must be a separate phase with a clear command or task name.

Example:

docs.title: Phase A: Fix N+1 Queries
docs.text: Run make task-run NAME=fix_n_plus_one after reviewing the report.

docs.title: Phase B: Remove Duplications
docs.text: Run make task-run NAME=remove_duplications with --priority --with-docs.

docs.title: Phase C: Add Missing Packages
docs.text: Execute: pip install django-extensions django-debug-toolbar

docs.title: Phase D: Create Base Code (if missing)
docs.text:
• Add a utils.py with helper functions.
  • Create a base template base.html if not present.
  • Add a custom context processor for shared variables.

docs.title: Phase 5: (Optional) Generate Base Code
docs.text: • If the analysis reveals missing foundational code (e.g., no utils.py, no base.html, no custom error pages), propose the content of those files in the report. - Do not write them automatically – ask the user to approve.

docs.title: Output Instructions
docs.text:
• After completing the analysis, save the report to ai/reports/ (create directory if needed).

  • Print a summary: “Report saved to …”.

  • Then ask: “Which recommended phase would you like to execute next? (Enter the phase letter, e.g., A)”

  • The user can then run the corresponding make task-run command or manual steps.

docs.title: Task: Fix N+1 Query Problems
docs.text:
Based on the analysis report (section 3), generate select_related/prefetch_related additions for each affected view.

For each issue: - Locate the queryset - Add .select_related('foreign_key_field') or .prefetch_related('reverse_relation') - Output the corrected code block with a # FIXED N+1 comment.

If the report is missing, ask the user to run analyze_project or comprehensive_analysis first.

docs.title: Task: Merge Code Styles (Context‑Aware)
docs.text:
You are a code style harmoniser. Given one or more input files (or a directory), analyse the coding style (indentation, quotes, line length, naming conventions) and merge them into a consistent style defined in .editorconfig or pyproject.toml.

Input context: Accepts file paths via @search or user selection. Output: Unified file(s) with a # MERGED header and a diff log.

If a conflict arises (e.g., different quote styles), ask the user for preference.

docs.title: Task: Refactor Use‑Case Variables (Context)
docs.text:
Analyse duplicated or misused context variables. Propose a centralised context processor or middleware.

Output required code and changes to existing views. Also check for over‑fetching and suggest caching.

docs.title: Task: Refactor to a Design Pattern
docs.text:
Analyse a set of files (or a module) and propose a refactoring to a specific OOP/design pattern: - Factory, Strategy, Observer, Repository, Service Layer, etc.

Input: User provides the target pattern and the files. Output: A step‑by‑step plan, plus code snippets. If approved, apply changes with a # REFACTORED comment.

docs.title: Task: Refactor Django Models
docs.text:
Examine models and suggest: - Database design improvements (indexes, field types) - Code clarity (verbose names, related_name) - Performance (select_related, custom managers) - Use of signals vs overridden save

Provide before/after code snippets.

docs.title: Task: Remove Code Duplications
docs.text:
Given the duplication report (section 2), propose a unified utility, template include, or JS module.

  • Python: extract to utils.py or a custom manager
  • Templates: create an include file (_shared.html)
  • JS: move to assets/js/modules/

Output a step‑by‑step plan and the new code.

docs.title: Task: Replace Pattern Across Files
docs.text:
You are a refactoring tool. Replace a given pattern (regex or string) in selected files with a new value. The user must provide: - Old pattern - New pattern - File glob (e.g., *.py) or explicit list

Safety: Create a backup of each changed file in ai/backups/ and output a summary of replacements.

docs.title: Task: Security Audit
docs.text:
Scan the Django project for: - Settings issues (DEBUG, SECRET_KEY, ALLOWED_HOSTS) - SQL injection (raw queries) - XSS (mark_safe, safe filter) - Command injection - Exposed secrets

List each finding with risk level and remediation.

docs.title: Task: Uniform Documentation
docs.text:
You are a technical writer. Make all documentation files in docs/ follow a consistent structure:

  1. YAML front matter (if used)
  2. Heading hierarchy (#, ##, ### – no skipping)
  3. Code blocks with language specifiers
  4. Relative links with descriptive text
  5. Admonitions using > 💡 Tip:, > ⚠️ Warning:, > ✅ Note:
  6. File naming: lowercase, underscores, no spaces

Output a table of changed files and what was modified.

docs.title: Task: Update Documentation from Code Changes
docs.text:
Review the latest git diff (or file changes) and update relevant .md files in docs/ to reflect code changes.

  • For each changed Python file, update API references.
  • For changed templates, update front‑end guides.
  • Add a changelog entry in docs/changelog.md.

Output a list of updated files.

docs.title: Task: Generate Django Tests
docs.text:
Given the models and views, generate pytest‑django tests for: - Model methods and validation - View status codes and templates - Forms and permissions

Output the test code as a ready‑to‑paste block.

docs.title: CTC Research — Asset & Media Architecture
docs.text:
Visual reference for how ctc-research.com frontend assets, static files, and media files flow from source code to the browser.

Date: 2026-07-12 Status: Current Companion guide: GUIDE.md

docs.title: 1. High-Level Asset Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Source
        A1[Django Templates]
        A2[SCSS / JS Sources]
    end

    subgraph Build
        B1[Webpack]
        B2[bundles.json]
        B3[collectstatic]
    end

    subgraph Serve
        C1[Traefik]
        C2[shared-media Nginx]
        C3[Django App]
    end

    subgraph Browser
        D1[HTML / CSS / JS]
    end

    A1 -->|{% render_bundle %}| B2
    A2 -->|import| B1
    B1 -->|hashed chunks| B2
    B2 -->|manifest| A1
    B1 --> B3
    B3 -->|staticfiles/| C2
    C1 -->|/static /media /sites| C2
    C1 -->|dynamic pages| C3
    C2 --> D1
    C3 --> D1

Explanation: 1. Developers write templates with {% render_bundle %} and SCSS/JS sources. 2. Webpack compiles sources into hashed chunks and writes bundles.json. 3. Django uses bundles.json to render the correct <script> / <link> tags. 4. collectstatic copies all static assets into staticfiles/. 5. Traefik routes static/media requests to the shared-media Nginx container. 6. Nginx serves files directly from the mounted volumes.

docs.title: CTC Research — Assets, Bundles & Shared Media Guide
docs.text:
How ctc-research.com loads its frontend assets, where static and media files live, and how the shared Nginx media server serves them.

Date: 2026-07-12 Status: Current Applies to: ctc-research.com, www.ctc-research.com, arch.ctc-research.com Related docs: - core/assets/ASSETS_GUIDE.md — shared frontend build system - core/ctc-research/assets/readme.md — per-site assets readme - docs/infrastructure/nginx/assets-configuration.md — Nginx static/media serving - ARCHITECTURE.md — visual architecture diagrams

docs.title: 1. Quick Summary
docs.text: Concern Path / Value Why Site directory core/ctc-research/ All CTC-specific code, templates, and assets Webpack entry (JS) core/ctc-research/assets/static/js/app.js Site-specific JS entry point Webpack entry (CSS) core/ctc-research/assets/static/js/static.js Imports main.scss to produce the CSS bundle Webpack output core/ctc-research/assets/bundles/ctc-research/ Hashed JS/CSS + bundles.json manifest Django STATIC_ROOT core/ctc-research/assets/staticfiles/ collectstatic destination Django STATIC_URL /static/ URL prefix for static files Django MEDIA_ROOT core/ctc-research/assets/media/ User-uploaded files on disk Django MEDIA_URL /media/ URL prefix for media files Shared media container shared-media (Nginx) Serves /static/ and /media/ for all sites Traefik media router media.ctc-research.com Dedicated hostname for CTC media

docs.title: 2. Template Bundle Tags
docs.text:
The shared base template at core/assets/templates/base.html loads the three canonical webpack chunks:

{% load webpack_loader %}

{# CSS in <head> #}
{% block css %}
    {% render_bundle 'static' 'css' %}
{% endblock %}

{# JS before </body> #}
{% render_bundle 'main' 'js' %}
{% render_bundle 'app' 'js' %}
Bundle Type Contents Source static CSS + JS Vendor CSS, site SCSS, tiny runtime shim ctc-research/assets/static/js/static.js → imports styles/main.scss main JS Shared core libraries (HTMX, Alpine, theme init) core/assets/static/js/core/main.js app JS CTC-specific logic and HTMX lifecycle bridge ctc-research/assets/static/js/app.js

docs.title: 2.1 What render_bundle produces
docs.text:
django-webpack-loader reads bundles.json (generated by webpack-bundle-tracker) and emits tags like:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/bundles/ctc-research/static-a1b2c3d4.css">
<script src="/static/bundles/ctc-research/main-e5f6g7h8.js"></script>
<script src="/static/bundles/ctc-research/app-i9j0k1l2.js"></script>

The BUNDLE_DIR_NAME setting is bundles/ctc-research/, so the final URL is always /static/bundles/ctc-research/<file>.

docs.title: 3. Webpack Build Flow
docs.text:
# Build CTC bundles (production)
npm --prefix core/assets run build:ctc

# Or from the site directory
cd core/ctc-research
make frontend-production

Under the hood:

  1. workspace.mjs resolves ctc → ctc-research.
  2. webpack/main.config.js sets:
  3. entry.app → ctc-research/assets/static/js/app.js
  4. entry.static → ctc-research/assets/static/js/static.js
  5. entry.main → core/assets/static/js/core/main.js
  6. output.path → ctc-research/assets/bundles/ctc-research/
  7. output.publicPath → /static/bundles/ctc-research/
  8. BundleTracker writes bundles.json in the same output directory.

docs.title: 3.1 Collectstatic
docs.text:
cd core/ctc-research
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

This copies: - Webpack bundles from assets/bundles/ctc-research/ → assets/staticfiles/bundles/ctc-research/ - Shared static sources from core/assets/static/ → assets/staticfiles/ - Site static sources from ctc-research/assets/static/ → assets/staticfiles/site/ctc-research/

docs.title: 3.2 Resulting static tree (simplified)
docs.text:
core/ctc-research/assets/staticfiles/
├── bundles/
│   └── ctc-research/
│       ├── bundles.json
│       ├── static-a1b2c3d4.css
│       ├── static-e5f6g7h8.js
│       ├── main-i9j0k1l2.js
│       └── app-j3k4l5m6.js
├── site/
│   └── ctc-research/
│       └── images/
│           └── logo.png
└── wagtailadmin/
    └── ...

docs.title: 4.1 Django settings
docs.text:
From core/configs/base/assets.py:

ASSETS_DIR = BASE_DIR / "assets"          # core/ctc-research/assets
MEDIA_DIR  = ASSETS_DIR / "media"          # core/ctc-research/assets/media
STATIC_DIR = ASSETS_DIR / "static"         # core/ctc-research/assets/static

MEDIA_ROOT = str(MEDIA_DIR)                # /app/ctc-research/assets/media
MEDIA_URL  = "/media/"

STATIC_ROOT = str(ASSETS_DIR / "staticfiles")  # /app/ctc-research/assets/staticfiles
STATIC_URL  = "/static/"

STATICFILES_DIRS = [
    ("bundles/ctc-research", "ctc-research/assets/bundles/ctc-research"),
    ("bundles/shared",       "core/assets/bundles/shared"),
    (None,                   "core/assets/static"),
    ("site/ctc-research",    "ctc-research/assets/static"),
]

docs.title: 4.2 URL-to-disk mapping
docs.text:
URL Disk path (inside container) Served by /static/bundles/ctc-research/static-a1b2c3d4.css /app/ctc-research/assets/staticfiles/bundles/ctc-research/static-a1b2c3d4.css Django dev server OR shared-media /static/images/logo.png /app/ctc-research/assets/staticfiles/site/ctc-research/images/logo.png shared-media /media/ctc-research/avatars/user1.png /app/ctc-research/assets/media/avatars/user1.png shared-media

In production, Traefik routes all /static/ and /media/ requests on ctc-research.com to the shared-media Nginx container, so Django never touches them.

docs.title: 5.1 Container mounts
docs.text:
From applications/proxy/docker-compose.nginx.yml:

services:
  shared-media:
    volumes:
      # Site build output staticfiles
      - ../core/ctc-research/assets/staticfiles:/var/www/sites/ctc-research/static:ro
      - ../core/lms-demo/assets/staticfiles:/var/www/sites/lms-demo/static:ro
      - ../core/VResume/assets/staticfiles:/var/www/sites/vresume/static:ro
      # Shared application static files
      - ../core/assets/static:/var/www/static:ro
      # Site-specific media uploads
      - ../core/ctc-research/assets/media:/var/www/media/ctc-research:ro
      - ../core/lms-demo/assets/media:/var/www/media/lms-demo:ro
      - ../core/VResume/assets/media:/var/www/media/vresume:ro

docs.title: 5.2 Nginx locations
docs.text:
From applications/proxy/nginx/default.conf:

# Webpack bundles (immutable, 1 year cache)
location /static/bundles/ctc-research/ {
    alias /var/www/sites/ctc-research/static/bundles/ctc-research/;
    expires 1y;
    add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
}

# Site-specific static files
location /sites/ctc-research/static/ {
    alias /var/www/sites/ctc-research/static/;
    expires 1y;
}

# Site-specific media files
location /media/ctc-research/ {
    alias /var/www/media/ctc-research/;
    expires 30d;
}

# Shared static / media fallbacks
location /static/ { alias /var/www/static/; }
location /media/  { alias /var/www/media/; }

docs.title: 5.3 Traefik routing
docs.text:
From applications/proxy/traefik/dynamic/ctc-research.yml:

http:
  routers:
    ctc-site-media-https:
      rule: >
        (Host(`ctc-research.com`) || Host(`www.ctc-research.com`) || Host(`arch.ctc-research.com`))
        && (PathPrefix(`/static/`) || PathPrefix(`/media/`) || PathPrefix(`/sites/`))
      entryPoints: [web-secure]
      service: ctc-site-media-service
      priority: 100
  services:
    ctc-site-media-service:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: 'http://shared-media:80'

And from applications/proxy/traefik/dynamic/media-servers.yml:

http:
  routers:
    ctc-media-https:
      rule: Host(`media.ctc-research.com`)
      entryPoints: [web-secure]
      service: ctc-media-service
      tls:
        certResolver: letsencrypt-http
  services:
    ctc-media-service:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: http://shared-media:80

docs.title: To Properly Load All Data
docs.text:
Create separate fixture files by model:

# Extract by model
python3 << 'EOF'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict

dump_file = Path("ctc-research/assets/fixtures/dump-data.json")
with open(dump_file) as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Group by model
by_model = defaultdict(list)
for item in data:
    model = item.get("model")
    by_model[model].append(item)

# Create individual fixture files
for model, items in by_model.items():
    filename = model.replace(".", "-") + ".json"
    filepath = Path(f"ctc-research/assets/fixtures/{filename}")
    with open(filepath, "w") as f:
        json.dump(items, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Created {filename}: {len(items)} objects")
EOF

docs.title: Alliance — Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide covers setting up a full local development environment using Docker Compose.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Requirement Minimum Version Docker 24.x Docker Compose 2.x (plugin) Git 2.x uv (Python package manager) 0.4+

Note: Python does not need to be installed on the host — everything runs inside containers. uv is only required if you plan to run management commands outside Docker.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone <your-repo-url> alliancecore
cd alliancecore/core

docs.title: 2. Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and edit it:

cp .env.example .env   # or use the existing .env as a base

docs.title: Required Variables
docs.text:
# Django
DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key-here
DJANGO_DEBUG=True
DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost,127.0.0.1

# Database (PostgreSQL)
DATABASE_URL=postgres://alliancecore:alliancecore@db:5432/alliancecore
POSTGRES_DB=alliancecore
POSTGRES_USER=alliancecore
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=alliancecore

# Redis
REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0

# Wagtail
WAGTAIL_SITE_NAME=Alliance

# Environment
DJANGO_ENV=local

docs.title: Optional Variables
docs.text:
# Email (development — console backend)
EMAIL_BACKEND=django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend

# Sentry (production only)
SENTRY_DSN=

# AWS S3 Storage (production only)
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=
AWS_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME=

# Temporal (background workflows)
TEMPORAL_ADDRESS=temporal:7233
TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE=default
TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE=alliancecore-tasks

# Stripe (payments)
STRIPE_PUBLIC_KEY=
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=

docs.title: 3. Set Up django-fusion (Source Clone)
docs.text:
Alliance uses django-fusion installed from a local source clone as configured in pyproject.toml:

[tool.uv.sources]
django-fusion = { path = "/libs/django-fusion", editable = true }

Clone django-fusion into the expected path:

# On your host machine (mounted into containers)
sudo mkdir -p /libs
cd /libs
git clone https://github.com/<org>/django-fusion.git

If you prefer a different path, update the path in pyproject.toml and the matching Docker volume mount in compose/.

docs.title: 4. Build and Start Services
docs.text:
# Build all images
docker compose build

# Start all services in the background
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Service Overview
docs.text: Service Purpose Port web Django (Gunicorn/Uvicorn) 8000 db PostgreSQL 5432 redis Cache + message broker 6379 nginx Static files + reverse proxy 80 worker Django RQ worker — temporal Temporal server 7233 temporal-ui Temporal web UI 8080 temporal-worker Temporal activity worker —

docs.title: Apply Migrations
docs.text: docker compose exec web python com migrate

docs.title: Load Initial Data (Optional)
docs.text: docker compose exec web python com loaddata dump-data.json

docs.title: Create Superuser
docs.text: docker compose exec web python com createsuperuser

docs.title: Compile Translations
docs.text: docker compose exec web django-admin compilemessages

docs.title: Build Frontend Assets
docs.text:
# Run inside the container (or locally if Node.js is installed)
docker compose exec web npm install
docker compose exec web npm run build

docs.title: 6. Access the Application
docs.text: Interface URL Main site http://localhost Django admin http://localhost/admin Wagtail admin http://localhost/cms API (Ninja) http://localhost/api/docs Temporal UI http://localhost:8080 Django Debug Toolbar Available in development

docs.title: Run the Development Server (without Docker)
docs.text:
# Install dependencies via uv
uv sync

# Start Django
python com runserver

docs.title: Frontend Hot Reload
docs.text:
npm run dev
# Webpack dev server at http://localhost:3000, proxies to Django at :8000

docs.title: Run Temporal Worker
docs.text: python com run_temporal_worker

docs.title: Run Tests
docs.text:
# Inside Docker
docker compose exec web pytest

# Locally
uv run pytest

docs.title: 8. Common Commands Reference
docs.text:
# Shorthand manage.py wrapper
python com <command>

# Examples
python com migrate
python com shell
python com shell_plus          # django-extensions
python com makemigrations
python com collectstatic
python com createsuperuser
python com run_temporal_worker
python com sync_alliancecore   # Alliance sync command

docs.title: 9. Stopping and Cleanup
docs.text:
# Stop services
docker compose down

# Stop and remove volumes (wipes database)
docker compose down -v

# Remove all built images
docker compose down --rmi all

docs.title: django-fusion not found
docs.text: Ensure /libs/django-fusion exists and is accessible inside the container via the volume mount. Check compose/ service definitions for the bind mount declaration.

docs.title: Database connection refused
docs.text: Verify DATABASE_URL matches the db service credentials in .env. Services sometimes need a few seconds to be ready; retry after docker compose up -d.

docs.title: Static files not loading
docs.text: Run python com collectstatic --noinput then reload Nginx: docker compose restart nginx.

docs.title: Migrations failing
docs.text: If you get integrity errors on a fresh install, try docker compose down -v to wipe the volume and start fresh.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The ContactSubmission model has been significantly enhanced with Wagtail integration, better field organization, and improved functionality. This document captures the analysis of the current implementation and recommendations for continued improvement.

docs.title: 1.1 Magic Strings and Hardcoded Values
docs.text:
Issue: Multiple hardcoded field names and magic strings throughout the code.

# Current problematic code
email_fields = ["email", "e_mail", "mail", "contact_email", "e-mail",
               "Email", "E-Mail", "EMAIL"]

Recommendation: Extract constants to class-level or module-level definitions.

class ContactSubmission(DefaultBase, DraftStateMixin, RevisionMixin, LockableMixin):
    EMAIL_FIELD_NAMES = [
        "email", "e_mail", "mail", "contact_email", "e-mail",
        "Email", "E-Mail", "EMAIL"
    ]
    NAME_FIELD_NAMES = ["name", "full_name", "fullname", "Full Name"]
    PHONE_FIELD_NAMES = [
        "phone", "telephone", "mobile", "phone_number",
        "Phone", "Telephone", "Mobile"
    ]

docs.title: 1.2 Repetitive Field Extraction Logic
docs.text:
Issue: Similar pattern repeated in get_email(), get_name(), and get_phone().

Recommendation: Create a generic field extraction method.

def _extract_field_value(self, field_names, transform_func=None):
    """Generic method to extract field values from submitted data."""
    for field in field_names:
        if value := self.submitted_data.get(field):
            result = str(value).strip()
            return transform_func(result) if transform_func else result
    return None

docs.title: 1.3 Long Method with Multiple Responsibilities
docs.text:
Issue: export_as_csv_row() handles both data transformation and flattening.

Recommendation: Split into separate methods for better single responsibility.

docs.title: 2.1 Strategy Pattern for Field Extraction
docs.text:
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

class FieldExtractor(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def extract(self, submitted_data: dict) -> str:
        pass

class EmailExtractor(FieldExtractor):
    def extract(self, submitted_data: dict) -> str:
        # Email extraction logic
        pass

docs.title: 2.2 Factory Pattern for Export Formats
docs.text:
class ExportFormatFactory:
    @staticmethod
    def create_exporter(format_type: str):
        if format_type == 'dict':
            return DictExporter()
        elif format_type == 'csv':
            return CSVExporter()

docs.title: 3.1 Import Organization
docs.text:
Recommended order (PEP 8):

# Standard library imports
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union

# Third-party imports
from django.db import models
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from modelcluster.models import ClusterableModel
from wagtail.admin.panels import FieldPanel, MultiFieldPanel, ObjectList, TabbedInterface
from wagtail.models import DraftStateMixin, LockableMixin, RevisionMixin

# Local imports
from django_fusion.pipelines.models import DefaultBase

docs.title: 3.2 Missing Type Hints
docs.text:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union, Any

def get_field_value(self, field_name: str) -> Optional[Any]:
    return self.submitted_data.get(field_name)

def get_email(self) -> Optional[str]: ...
def export_as_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: ...

docs.title: 3.3 Inconsistent Error Handling
docs.text:
import logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def get_preview_url(self) -> Optional[str]:
    if not self.page_id:
        return None
    try:
        from wagtail.models import Page
        page = Page.objects.get(id=self.page_id)
        return page.get_full_url()
    except Page.DoesNotExist:
        logger.warning(f"Page with ID {self.page_id} not found for submission {self.id}")
        return None
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error getting preview URL for submission {self.id}: {e}")
        return None

docs.title: 4.1 Method Documentation
docs.text:
def mark_as_processed(self) -> None:
    """
    Mark this submission as processed and set the processed date.

    Updates the processed flag to True and sets processed_date to current time.
    Only updates the necessary fields to avoid unnecessary database writes.

    Raises:
        DatabaseError: If the update operation fails.
    """
    from django.utils import timezone
    self.processed = True
    self.processed_date = timezone.now()
    self.save(update_fields=["processed", "processed_date", "updated_at"])

docs.title: 4.2 Complex Logic Simplification
docs.text:
def get_name(self) -> str:
    direct_name = self._get_direct_name()
    if direct_name:
        return direct_name
    combined_name = self._get_combined_name()
    if combined_name:
        return combined_name
    return _("Anonymous")

def _get_direct_name(self) -> Optional[str]:
    return self._extract_field_value(self.NAME_FIELD_NAMES)

def _get_combined_name(self) -> Optional[str]:
    first_name = self.submitted_data.get("first_name", "").strip()
    last_name = self.submitted_data.get("last_name", "").strip()
    if first_name or last_name:
        return f"{first_name} {last_name}".strip()
    return None

docs.title: 5.2 Validation Methods
docs.text:
def clean(self) -> None:
    super().clean()
    self._validate_submitted_data()
    self._validate_page_reference()

def _validate_submitted_data(self) -> None:
    if not isinstance(self.submitted_data, dict):
        raise ValidationError(_("Submitted data must be a dictionary"))
    if not self.submitted_data:
        raise ValidationError(_("Submitted data cannot be empty"))

docs.title: 6.1 Database Query Caching
docs.text:
from django.core.cache import cache

def get_preview_url(self) -> Optional[str]:
    if not self.page_id:
        return None
    cache_key = f"submission_preview_url_{self.page_id}"
    cached_url = cache.get(cache_key)
    if cached_url is not None:
        return cached_url
    try:
        from wagtail.models import Page
        page = Page.objects.get(id=self.page_id)
        url = page.get_full_url()
        cache.set(cache_key, url, timeout=3600)
        return url
    except Page.DoesNotExist:
        cache.set(cache_key, None, timeout=300)
        return None

docs.title: 6.2 Bulk Operations Support
docs.text:
@classmethod
def bulk_mark_processed(cls, submission_ids: List[int]) -> int:
    from django.utils import timezone
    return cls.objects.filter(
        id__in=submission_ids,
        processed=False
    ).update(
        processed=True,
        processed_date=timezone.now()
    )

docs.title: 7.1 Data Sanitization
docs.text:
import bleach

def sanitize_submitted_data(self) -> None:
    if isinstance(self.submitted_data, dict):
        self.submitted_data = self._sanitize_dict(self.submitted_data)

def _sanitize_dict(self, data: dict) -> dict:
    sanitized = {}
    for key, value in data.items():
        if isinstance(value, str):
            sanitized[key] = bleach.clean(value, strip=True)
        elif isinstance(value, dict):
            sanitized[key] = self._sanitize_dict(value)
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            sanitized[key] = [
                bleach.clean(item, strip=True) if isinstance(item, str) else item
                for item in value
            ]
        else:
            sanitized[key] = value
    return sanitized

class ContactSubmissionManager(models.Manager):
    def processed(self):
        return self.filter(processed=True)

    def pending(self):
        return self.filter(processed=False)

    def by_form(self, form_id: str):
        return self.filter(form_id=form_id)

    def recent(self, days: int = 7):
        from django.utils import timezone
        from datetime import timedelta
        cutoff_date = timezone.now() - timedelta(days=days)
        return self.filter(submission_date__gte=cutoff_date)

objects = ContactSubmissionManager()

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document describes the JavaScript module architecture for Alliance. The architecture is designed for modularity, dynamic loading, and centralized configuration.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
assets/static/js/
├── main.js              # Entry point — loads libraries and initializes app
├── app.js               # Application class with core functionality
├── registry.js          # Unified registry for services and infrastructure
├── init.config.js       # Centralized configuration and page detection
├── config.helpers.js    # Logic for layout and page type detection
│
├── utility/             # Core utilities
│   ├── base.manager.js  # Base class for all managers
│   ├── dom.js           # DOM manipulation helpers
│   ├── helpers.js       # General utility functions
│   ├── state.js         # State management
│   └── index.js         # Utility exports
│
├── modules/             # Feature modules
│   ├── manager.init.js  # ModuleManager — handles dynamic module loading
│   ├── index.js         # Module exports
│   ├── components/      # UI components
│   │   ├── manager.init.js  # UIManager — handles UI component lifecycle
│   │   ├── docs/            # Component documentation
│   │   └── index.js
│   ├── handlers/        # Service handlers (Events, Cookies, SSE)
│   ├── forms/           # Form handling logic
│   ├── navigations/     # Navigation tracking
│   └── notifications/   # Notification system (Toast, Alert, SSE)
│
└── plugins/             # Optional plugins
    └── backgroundImages.js

docs.title: Initialization Flow
docs.text:
1. Browser loads main.js
  2. Imports external libraries (jQuery, Bootstrap, AlpineJS, etc.)
  3. Imports CONFIG from init.config.js (starts auto-detection)

  4. Imports app singleton from app.js

  5. DOMContentLoaded

  6. main.js calls initialize()

  7. app.init() is called, which:

    • Initializes URL tracking
    • Sets up core event listeners
    • Automatically initializes uiManager and registry

  8. Registry & Component Discovery

  9. registry.init(): Initializes core services — Events, Cookies, SSE
  10. uiManager.init(): Scans the DOM for components (defined in UI_COMPONENTS) and initializes them

docs.title: Application (app.js)
docs.text: The main orchestrator. Manages the high-level lifecycle and coordinates between managers. - Singleton: app - Responsibilities: Error handling, global event coordination

docs.title: RegistryManager (registry.js)
docs.text: Unified registry for infrastructure services. - Singleton: registry - Core Services: events, cookies, sse, notifications - Logic: Handles dynamic service loading from the handlers/ directory

docs.title: ModuleManager (modules/manager.init.js)
docs.text: Handles dynamic module loading with dependency resolution and retry logic. - Singleton: moduleManager - Key Methods: registerModule(), load(), getModule()

docs.title: UIManager (modules/components/manager.init.js)
docs.text: Manages the lifecycle of UI components (sliders, tabs, modals, etc.). - Singleton: uiManager - Key Methods: initComponents(), refreshAll()

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration is centralized in init.config.js via the CONFIG object:

Key Purpose layout Automatic page and layout detection settings security CSRF and cookie configurations sse / notifications Real-time update settings modules Dependency maps and loading orders preloader Configuration for the page loading screen page (Runtime) Detected page type and discovered components

docs.title: Adding a Service
docs.text:
1. Create a handler class in modules/handlers/
  2. Register it in registry.js under the services configuration

docs.title: Adding a Component
docs.text:
1. Create a component class in modules/components/
  2. Register it in the UI_COMPONENTS map within modules/components/manager.init.js
  3. Define its CSS selectors for auto-detection

docs.title: Global Access (Development)
docs.text:
window.app         // Application instance
window.registry    // Infrastructure registry
window.uiManager   // UI component manager
window.APP_CONFIG  // Active configuration

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document outlines the structure, flow, and usage of the JavaScript codebase in assets/static/js.

docs.title: Core System
docs.text: The core system is built around init.layout.js (Unified Page & Layout Management System).

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• init.layout.js — [USED] Core file containing PagesManager, BaseLayout, LayoutManager.
  • Classes:
    • PagesManager: URL, parameters, and page info tracking
    • BaseLayout: Parent class for all layouts (notifications, navigation)
    • LayoutManager: Handles layout detection and dynamic loading

  • Restored from init.layout.orig.js

  • app.js — [USED] Main application entry point (Application class).

  • Key Methods:
    • init(): Bootstrap application
    • handleURLChange(): Route changes
    • handleError(): Global error handling

docs.title: PagesManager
docs.text: Method Status Description initialize(options) [USED] Starts URL tracking. Called on DOM ready getParameter(key, defaultValue) [USED] Retrieves URL parameters setParameter(key, value) [USED] Sets URL parameters and updates the URL updateURL() [USED] Syncs state to the browser URL bar extractPageInfo() [USED] Reads metadata from the DOM

docs.title: BaseLayout
docs.text: Method Status Description init() [USED] Initializer for layout systems apply(layoutType, data) [USED] Applies specific layout configuration and classes showNotification(msg, type) [USED] Displays UI notifications createFallbackNotificationSystem() [FALLBACK] Only used if no other system exists

docs.title: LayoutManager
docs.text: Method Status Description initialize(app) [USED] Detects and loads the initial layout detectLayout() [USED] Determines the current layout from URL/DOM loadLayout(name) [USED] Dynamically imports and instantiates layout files switchLayout(name) [USED] Unloads current layout and loads a new one

docs.title: Other Core Files
docs.text:
• main.js — [USED] Webpack entry point. Imports libraries and initializes app.js
  • static.js — [USED] Bundle entry point. Imports CSS and main.js
  • init.config.js — [USED] Configuration settings (CONFIG object)

docs.title: Layouts (pages/)
docs.text:
All layouts extend BaseLayout from init.layout.js.

File Status Description app.layout.js [USED] Main dashboard/app layout. Handles sidebar, panels, widgets auth.layout.js [USED] Authentication pages (login, register) landing.layout.js [USED] Public landing pages profile.layout.js [USED] User profile pages notifications.layout.js [USED] Notification handling init.layout.orig.js [BACKUP] Backup — not used in production

docs.title: Utilities (utility/)
docs.text: File Status Description base.manager.js [USED] Base class for managers dom.js [USED] DOM manipulation helpers (DOM object) helpers.js [USED] General utilities (Utils object) url.js [USED] URL tracking mixin app.metrics.js [USED] Performance metrics

docs.title: Modules (modules/)
docs.text: Structured module system. - index.js: Exports moduleManager

docs.title: Application Flow
docs.text:
Browser → static.js → main.js → app.init()
                                    ↓
                            init.layout.js (auto-init on DOM ready)
                                    ↓
                            layoutManager.detectLayout()
                                    ↓
                            layoutManager.loadLayout('app' | 'auth' | ...)
                                    ↓
                            layout.init() → layout.apply()

docs.title: Preloader Component
docs.text: The Preloader component provides a loading screen while page assets are fetching. It supports multiple predefined types and automatically initializes based on the data-preloader attribute on the <body> tag.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Enable the preloader by adding data-preloader="TYPE" to your <body> tag:

<body data-preloader="1">
    <!-- Body content -->
</body>

docs.title: Preloader Types
docs.text: Type data-preloader Description Type 1 "1" Circular SVG loader with a progress bar Type 2 "2" Spinner animation with a progress bar Type 3 "3" Three-dot bouncing animation with a progress bar

docs.title: CSS Customization
docs.text:
Customize appearance via CSS variables:

:root {
  /* Circular Preloader */
  --preloader-bg: var(--theme-bg-primary);             /* Overlay background */
  --preloader-path-color: var(--theme-primary);        /* Circular path color */
  --preloader-progress-color: var(--theme-text-tertiary); /* Progress text */

  /* Three-Dot Loading */
  --three-dot-object-color: var(--theme-secondary);    /* Dot color */

  /* Transition Speed */
  --preloader-transition: opacity 0.5s ease;
}

docs.title: JavaScript API
docs.text:
The Preloader class is exported from preloader.init.js:

import { Preloader } from './partials/preloader.init.js';

const loader = new Preloader();
loader.init();

// Manually show/hide
loader.show(); // Removes .loaded class from body
loader.hide(); // Adds .loaded class to body

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: Aspect Detail Initialization Auto-initialized by UIManager when [data-preloader] is detected on the page DOM Structure Dynamically injected into <body> based on selected type Hide Trigger Listens for window.load event Fallback 3000ms timeout hides the preloader regardless of load state Progress Tracking Uses the Performance API to estimate resource loading progress

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution Preloader not showing Ensure data-preloader attribute is present on <body> Preloader stuck Check window.load is firing; fallback hides it after 3 seconds

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Alliance is designed to be fully integrated with AI-driven development workflows using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP allows AI agents (like Claude or Antigravity) to act as a "junior developer" with direct access to your Django environment.

docs.title: 🛠️ Usage with Django Grep
docs.text: The django-fusion plugin provides the underlying server that implements the MCP tools. It is installed as a source clone at /libs/django-fusion (see INSTALL.md).

docs.title: Available Tools
docs.text: Tool Description search_code Fast regex search across the entire project design_component Create new Wagtail blocks and templates autonomously inspect_schema Visualize database relationships and model definitions debug_logs Access and analyze application logs in real-time

docs.title: 🔌 How to Integrate
docs.text:
To enable AI agents to work on this project:

  1. Ensure django_fusion.mcp_designer is in INSTALLED_APPS.
  2. Configure your AI IDE (e.g., Cursor, Windsurf) or Agent to point to the mcp_django_server.py entry point.
  3. Use the following prompt to prime the AI:

    "You are an expert Django/Wagtail developer. Use the MCP tools provided by django-fusion to explore the Alliance codebase and help me build new features."

docs.title: 📍 Integration Points
docs.text:
• Core: The core project provides the settings and structure for MCP discovery.
  • Plugins: Each plugin (Blog, Handlers) contains its own logic that the AI can discover and extend.
  • LMS: When the LMS module is active, AI agents will automatically scan its models and offer LMS-specific tools.

INSTALLED_APPS = [

]

docs.title: Traefik Certificate Backup & Restoration System
docs.text: Purpose: Automatically backup and restore SSL/TLS certificates managed by Traefik's ACME configuration.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Backup current certificates
./cert-backup.sh backup

# List all backups
./cert-backup.sh list

# Restore from a backup
./cert-backup.sh restore /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/20260602_121530_certs

# View status
./cert-backup.sh status

# Cleanup old backups (keep last 10)
./cert-backup.sh cleanup 10

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
/root/site/websites/compose/traefik/
├── acme/                          # Traefik ACME directory (active certificates)
│   └── acme.json                  # Certificate store (generated by Traefik)
├── certs/                  # Backup directory
│   ├── 20260602_120530_certs/     # Backup 1 (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS format)
│   │   ├── acme.json              # Backed up certificate file
│   │   └── backup-metadata.txt    # Backup info & timestamp
│   ├── 20260602_130045_certs/     # Backup 2
│   │   ├── acme.json
│   │   └── backup-metadata.txt
│   └── pre-restore_1717XXX_certs/ # Safety backups (before restore operations)
├── cert-backup.sh                 # This backup script
├── traefik.yml                    # Traefik configuration
├── dynamic/                       # Dynamic routing config
└── Dockerfile                     # Traefik Docker image

docs.title: Manual Backup
docs.text:
cd /root/site/websites/compose/traefik
./cert-backup.sh backup

Output: - Creates dated directory: certs/YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_certs/ - Copies acme.json with all certificates - Generates backup-metadata.txt with: - Backup timestamp - File list and sizes - Certificate domain information (if jq available) - Expiry dates

Example Backup Directory: 

certs/20260602_145230_certs/
├── acme.json                    (12.4 KB)
└── backup-metadata.txt          (1.8 KB)

Content of backup-metadata.txt:
  Traefik Certificate Backup
  ==========================
  Backup Date: 2026-06-02 14:52:30
  Timestamp: 20260602_145230
  Source Directory: /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/acme
  Backup Directory: /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/20260602_145230_certs

  Files Backed Up:
  -rw------- 1 root root 12.4K Jun  2 14:52 acme.json
  -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1.8K Jun  2 14:52 backup-metadata.txt

  Certificate Information:
  Domain: ctc-research.com, Expiry: 2026-09-02T10:23:45Z
  Domain: structa.cloud, Expiry: 2026-09-02T10:24:15Z
  Domain: vresume.structa.cloud, Expiry: 2026-09-02T10:25:00Z

docs.title: Automatic Backup (Cron Job)
docs.text:
Setup Daily Backup at 2 AM: 

# Edit crontab
crontab -e

# Add this line (runs daily at 2:00 AM)
0 2 * * * cd /root/site/websites/compose/traefik && ./cert-backup.sh backup >> /var/log/traefik-backup.log 2>&1

# Or for every 6 hours
0 */6 * * * cd /root/site/websites/compose/traefik && ./cert-backup.sh backup >> /var/log/traefik-backup.log 2>&1

Verify Cron Job: 

# View installed cron jobs
crontab -l

# Check backup log
tail -f /var/log/traefik-backup.log

# Manually trigger backup (test)
cd /root/site/websites/compose/traefik && ./cert-backup.sh backup

docs.title: Restore from Backup
docs.text:
# 1. List available backups
./cert-backup.sh list

# 2. Choose a backup and restore it
./cert-backup.sh restore /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/20260602_145230_certs

# 3. Restart Traefik to apply new certificates
docker compose restart traefik

# 4. Verify certificates loaded
docker compose logs traefik --tail 50

docs.title: Restoration Process
docs.text:
1. Safety Backup: Before restoring, current certificates are backed up to pre-restore_<timestamp>_certs/
  2. File Restore: Backup's acme.json copied to /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/acme/
  3. Permissions: File permissions set to 600 (read/write for owner only)
  4. Service Restart: Traefik must be restarted to reload certificates

docs.title: Restore from Emergency Pre-Restore Backup
docs.text:
# If something went wrong after restore, use the pre-restore backup
./cert-backup.sh restore /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/pre-restore_1717XXX_certs

# Restart Traefik
docker compose restart traefik

docs.title: List Backups
docs.text:
./cert-backup.sh list

Output Example:

1. 20260602_145230_certs (12.5 KB)
   Created: 2026-06-02 14:52:30
   Domain: ctc-research.com, Expiry: 2026-09-02T10:23:45Z
2. 20260602_120045_certs (12.4 KB)
   Created: 2026-06-02 12:00:45
   Domain: ctc-research.com, Expiry: 2026-09-02T10:23:45Z
3. 20260601_200530_certs (12.2 KB)
   Created: 2026-06-01 20:05:30
   Domain: ctc-research.com, Expiry: 2026-09-02T10:23:45Z

✓ Total backups: 3

docs.text:
# Keep only the last 10 backups (removes older ones)
./cert-backup.sh cleanup 10

# Keep only the last 5 backups
./cert-backup.sh cleanup 5

# Default is 10 if not specified
./cert-backup.sh cleanup

[12:34:56] Found 15 backups. Removing oldest...
[12:34:56] Removing: 20260525_020000_certs (12.3 KB)
[12:34:56] Removing: 20260524_020000_certs (12.1 KB)
[12:34:56] Removing: 20260523_020000_certs (12.5 KB)
[12:34:56] Removing: 20260522_020000_certs (12.4 KB)
[12:34:56] Removing: 20260521_020000_certs (12.2 KB)
✓ Cleanup complete. Kept last 10 backups.

docs.title: Scenario 1: Lost All Certificates
docs.text:
Problem: The acme.json file got corrupted or deleted, certificates no longer work.

Solution: 

# 1. Restore from latest backup
./cert-backup.sh list
./cert-backup.sh restore /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/20260602_145230_certs

# 2. Restart Traefik
docker compose restart traefik

# 3. Verify certificates are loaded
docker compose logs traefik --tail 50 | grep -i "certificate\|error"

docs.title: Scenario 2: Bad Restore - Need to Rollback
docs.text:
Problem: Restored wrong backup and websites are down.

Solution: 

# 1. Safety backup from failed restore is automatically created
ls -la /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/pre-restore_*

# 2. Restore from the pre-restore backup
./cert-backup.sh restore /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/pre-restore_1717XXX_certs

# 3. Restart Traefik
docker compose restart traefik

docs.title: Scenario 3: Expired Certificates
docs.text:
Problem: All certificates have expired, Let's Encrypt rejected renewal.

Solution: 

# 1. Save current (expired) certs for reference
./cert-backup.sh backup

# 2. Delete the corrupted acme.json to force renewal
rm /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/acme/acme.json

# 3. Restart Traefik (it will request new certs)
docker compose restart traefik

# 4. Monitor renewal process
docker compose logs traefik -f --tail 50

# 5. Once successful, backup new certificates
./cert-backup.sh backup

docs.title: Scenario 4: Certificate Storage Full
docs.text:
Problem: Too many backups taking up disk space.

Solution: 

# 1. Check current usage
./cert-backup.sh status

# 2. Remove old backups, keep only recent ones
./cert-backup.sh cleanup 5

# 3. Verify cleanup
./cert-backup.sh list

docs.title: Backup During Container Deployment
docs.text:
Add to docker-compose.yml post-deployment: 

# After 'docker compose up -d' completes
post_deployment:
  - command: 'cd /root/site/websites/compose/traefik && ./cert-backup.sh backup'
    description: 'Backup new certificates after successful deployment'

docs.title: Backup on Container Restart
docs.text:
The Traefik container in the docker-compose.yml should have restart policy: 

traefik:
  restart: unless-stopped
  # After restart completes and certs are loaded:
  # - Certificates are automatically reloaded
  # - Run backup: ./cert-backup.sh backup

docs.title: Check Backup Age
docs.text:
# List backups sorted by date
ls -ltr /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/*/backup-metadata.txt

# Find backups older than 7 days
find /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs -type d -mtime +7 -name "*_certs"

docs.title: Alert if No Recent Backup
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Check if latest backup is older than 24 hours
LATEST_BACKUP=$(ls -t /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/certs/*/backup-metadata.txt | head -1)
LATEST_TIME=$(stat -c %Y "$LATEST_BACKUP")
NOW=$(date +%s)
DIFF=$((NOW - LATEST_TIME))
THRESHOLD=$((24 * 60 * 60))  # 24 hours

if [ $DIFF -gt $THRESHOLD ]; then
  echo "WARNING: Certificate backup is older than 24 hours!"
  # Send alert, create ticket, etc.
fi

docs.title: Backup Failed: "No acme.json found"
docs.text:
Cause: Traefik hasn't generated certificates yet. Fix: 

# Wait for Traefik to generate certificates
docker compose logs traefik -f | grep -i "certificate\|acme"

# Once certificates are generated, retry backup
./cert-backup.sh backup

docs.title: Restore Failed: "Permission denied"
docs.text:
Cause: Need write permissions to acme directory. Fix: 

# Check permissions
ls -la /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/acme/

# If needed, fix permissions
chmod 700 /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/acme/
chmod 600 /root/site/websites/compose/traefik/acme/acme.json

docs.title: Traefik Not Loading Restored Certs
docs.text:
Cause: Traefik needs restart to reload certificates. Fix: 

# Restart Traefik
docker compose restart traefik

# Wait for startup and verify
sleep 10
docker compose logs traefik --tail 30 | grep -i "certificate\|loaded"

# Test HTTPS access
curl -I https://ctc-research.com/
curl -I https://structa.cloud/
curl -I https://vresume.structa.cloud/

docs.title: jq Not Available (Certificate Info Missing)
docs.text:
Cause: jq JSON processor not installed in container/host. Fix: 

# Install jq (on Linux)
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq

# Or in Docker container
docker exec traefik apt-get update && docker exec traefik apt-get install -y jq

# Retry backup to get certificate info
./cert-backup.sh backup

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Regular Backups: Setup daily automated backups via cron
  2. Keep History: Maintain last 10-20 backups for safety

  5. Document Changes: Note what was in each backup (already done in metadata)
  6. Cleanup Regularly: Remove old backups to save disk space
  7. Verify After Restore: Always test HTTPS connectivity after restore

docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Slider Navigator: Fixed duplicate refreshAll() method that shadowed the async destroy+reinit version, causing slides to not re-initialize after HTMX navigation
  • Slider Swiper Dual-loading: Added early-return in loadDependencies() when Swiper is already bundled via Webpack (avoids wasted CDN fallback)
  • Sidebar Toggle (Mobile): Added sidebar--active class toggle to expand parent max-height — sidebar content was clipped at 180px even when .sidebar__more.open expanded
  • Unified Modal Display: Fixed component never initializing — selectors [data-modal-trigger]/[data-htmx-modal] didn't match any DOM elements. Added #unified-modal-overlay and [data-modal-overlay] to selectors
  • Unified Modal Close: Modal now clears stale content from container on close
  • Preloader Memory Leak: showHTMXPreloader() now removes stale Map entries before creating new ones, with requestAnimationFrame for proper transition
  • Tag Filter Listener Leak: Fixed bindEvents() using anonymous arrow functions that couldn't be cleaned up. Now uses stored bound handler references
  • DOM Cache Fragmentation: Removed duplicate clearCache()/invalidateCache() methods that appeared twice in dom.js
  • DOM Global Access: window.DOM now always available (was conditional on CONFIG.debug), fixing cache invalidation failing in production
  • Component Double-init Guard: Added data-{componentId}-init marker to prevent duplicate component instances on HTMX swaps
  • N+1 Database Queries: Added select_related/prefetch_related to blog and project detail views
  • Cookie Consent: SessionStorage tracking ensures dialog shows only once per browsing session
  • Theme Hover Colors: Replaced hardcoded rgba(238, 155, 0, ...) with var(--color-accent-rgb) for theme-adaptive hover effects
  • Documentation: Fixed Tailwind CSS v4 reference → correct Bootstrap 5/SCSS stack in architecture docs

docs.title: Phase B: SSL Certificate Management (30 min)
B1: Create Backup Script
docs.text:
File: compose/traefik/scripts/backup-certs.sh 

#!/bin/bash
# Backup SSL certificates

BACKUP_DIR="/etc/traefik/acme/backups"
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
cp /etc/traefik/acme/acme.json "$BACKUP_DIR/acme_$TIMESTAMP.json"
echo "Backup completed: $BACKUP_DIR/acme_$TIMESTAMP.json"

docs.title: B2: Create Restore Script
docs.text:
File: compose/traefik/scripts/restore-certs.sh 

#!/bin/bash
# Restore SSL certificates if they don't exist

ACME_FILE="/etc/traefik/acme/acme.json"
BACKUP_DIR="/etc/traefik/acme/backups"

if [ ! -f "$ACME_FILE" ]; then
    if [ -f "$BACKUP_DIR"/acme_*.json ]; then
        LATEST=$(ls -t "$BACKUP_DIR"/acme_*.json | head -n1)
        cp "$LATEST" "$ACME_FILE"
        chmod 600 "$ACME_FILE"
        echo "Restored certificates from: $LATEST"
    else
        echo "No backup found, will generate new certificates"
    fi
fi

docs.title: B3: Update Traefik Dockerfile
docs.text:
File: compose/traefik/Dockerfile 

FROM traefik:latest

COPY scripts/backup-certs.sh /backup-certs.sh
COPY scripts/restore-certs.sh /restore-certs.sh
RUN chmod +x /backup-certs.sh /restore-certs.sh

# Run on startup
ENTRYPOINT ["/restore-certs.sh"]
CMD ["traefik", "--configFile=/etc/traefik/traefik.yml"]

docs.title: C1: Create Consolidation Script
